candidates.tagline: The upgrade was supposed to modernize US air traffic control. It stopped all of it instead.
candidates.story: On November 13, 2026, defense contractor L3Harris triggered the second-ever nationwide US aviation ground stop since 9/11 while replacing the FAA's copper-wire telecom backbone with fiber; a router being swapped out flooded the air traffic control network with over 1,000 connection attempts per second, collapsing the system. About 25,000 flights were delayed and 9,000+ cancelled. Transportation Secretary Duffy said the FAA 'is using old equipment.' The first nationwide ground stop since 9/11 — in 2023 — was also caused by contractor error at an FAA system. A 2023 safety review had already warned the network relied on 'obsolete telecommunications technology.'
candidates.why_funny: The agency responsible for keeping every US flight safe was already warned in writing that its telecom system was dangerously obsolete — then grounded the entire country during a routine upgrade of the very system it already knew was fragile.
candidates.alt: The FAA air traffic control tower at Philadelphia International Airport rising above the terminal buildings — identical in design to the towers whose copper-wire telecom backbone was being upgraded when a router collapse triggered a nationwide ground stop on November 13, 2026

candidates.tagline: The company behind Transformers transformed their logo into something nobody recognizes.
candidates.story: On November 9, 2026, Takara Tomy — Japan's largest toy company, co-creator of Transformers, and licensed maker of Beyblades and Pokémon products — announced its first corporate rebrand since the 2006 Takara–TOMY merger: a new abstract gradient symbol based on Japanese katakana for 'asobi' (play), replacing the simple recognizable TOMY wordmark globally from April 1, 2027. The move also renames the company to TAKARATOMY Corporation. Design outlet Creative Bloq headlined its coverage: 'The toy company Tomy has a new logo, and people are baffled.'
candidates.why_funny: The company that makes Transformers — toys whose entire concept is 'changes into something nobody recognises' — applied that exact transformation to their own logo, effective April Fools' Day.
candidates.alt: A red Optimus Prime Transformers truck at Hamleys toy store's London parade — one of the flagship products made by Takara Tomy, now rebranding to TAKARATOMY Corporation with a gradient abstract logo that leaves international markets baffled
